transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood Partnerships), Priya Kapoor (Acme Channel Lead), Liam O'Connor (Acme Sales Director), Samira Ahmed (Acme TPM)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Partner co-selling pipeline review: Acme will help introduce Redwood to three priority accounts in Q1; Redwood will provide benchmarks, a co-sell GTM one-pager, and flexible pricing for pilot deals.
- Technical follow-ups: SE-led benchmark on performance and latency on Acme-managed infra, SOC2/security playbook share.
- Commercial: outline partner discount tiers and revenue split; agree on joint exec intro cadence.

Topics: co-sell strategy, target accounts, pilot scoping, pricing/discounts, security/compliance, next steps and owners.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour so i'll run through the agenda real quick. Jordan, maya, carlos from Redwood and priya, liam, samira from acme. sound right?
[00:15] Priya (Acme): yep that's right, thanks jordan. quick note — we have someone joining late but they said it's fine to start.
[00:22] Jordan: great. agenda — quick pipeline review, target accounts, what success looks like for acme + redwood co-sell, technical asks, and then next steps. any changes?
[00:33] Liam (Acme): no that's good. we just want to make sure the pricing and pilot mechanics are clear. we've had some pushback historically around how credits and discounts line up.
[00:44] Carlos (Redwood Partnerships): yeah i'll cover partner portal and visibility later. first, priya did you want to confirm the three accounts you mentioned in the email?
[00:55] Priya: sure — bankcorp, medibase, and retailworks. bankcorp is high-touch (SaaS security reqs), medibase is data-sensitive and needs on-prem options, retailworks is very latency-sensitive. all three are good candidates for a pilot.
[01:12] Maya (Redwood SE): quick Q — when you say on-prem for medibase, do you mean fully air-gapped or just VPC/private deployment? sometimes acme says air-gapped but it's actually a VPC peering.
[01:27] Priya: good call — it's VPC peering but they have strict KMS requirements and want audit-level logs. not air-gapped.
[01:36] Samira (Acme TPM): and retailworks will probably want a dedicated pool, they have 99.9 latency SLOs for checkout flows.
[01:46] Jordan: ok so we have a mix — security heavy, VPC and KMS, and latency heavy. that's actually a good spread to show— we can demonstrate hosted + private options.
[01:57] Liam: what's the typical timeline we should tell them for a pilot? two to four weeks?
[02:03] Maya: for a basic hosted pilot, 1-2 weeks to onboard and validate. for a dedicated or VPC setup, usually 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup.
[02:15] Priya: perfect. for bankcorp we'll need to show SOC2 docs and maybe do a short security deep-dive. can you share that?
[02:22] Jordan: yeah we'll share our SOC2 and security playbook. caveat — sometimes the auto-transcription label has 's0c two' which is weird but we'll send PDFs.
[02:33] Carlos: i'll make sure the partner portal has a place for those artifacts and set permissions for bankcorp. also i'll add pipeline visibility so we can track accounts in the portal.
[02:45] Priya: great. on pricing, we need a partner discount that makes our pitch competitive. what are your typical partner tiers?
[02:53] Jordan: we have a standard partner discount and a co-sell discount for joint-sourced deals. i'll send the grid — short answer: 10% retail discount for partners, 20% for co-sell verified pipeline plus revenue share options.
[03:08] Liam: that helps. is any of that negotiable per account? bankcorp might want enterprise terms.
[03:15] Jordan: yes for enterprise we can do bespoke pricing — often tied to committed usage (e.g., dedicated monthly commit). we'll figure that in the commercial pilot SOW.
[03:26] Samira: about the commercial pilot — do you have a template SOW that includes P0 success metrics?
[03:33] Carlos: yes we have a partner SOW template, i'll attach it in the portal. it's usually simple: scope, duration, success criteria (throughput, latency targets, data residency), and exit criteria.
[03:44] Maya: from a technical standpoint i'd like to suggest we run a quick benchmark of a 10k token chat sim and a 1k token rerank workload to show token/p95 latency on our hosted vs a VPC setup. that should give acme confidence on cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:59] Priya: sounds good. will you need access to any of our infra for that?
[04:04] Maya: ideally we'd run with simulated traffic first on our side; for the VPC test we might need network peering and an IAM/KMS contact. we can also do a runbook to minimize security exposure.
[04:16] Priya: i'll coordinate that with samira.
[04:19] [00:04:20] Jordan: quick aside — competitors were mentioned earlier in our internal thread; acme flagged anthropic because they like the safety positioning. we should prepare a short comparison.
[04:34] Liam: yep anthropic comes up. also, some accounts are looking at databricks for embeddings pipelines, and pinecone for vector search. our angle is that redwood plugs into their stack and reduces inference ops burden.
[04:47] Jordan: exactly. our pitch is 'reduce ops, predictable latency and cost, same API across hosted/dedicated/private'. we'll provide a two-slide summary for reps.
[04:59] Priya: can we see a sample rep-facing one-pager?
[05:02] Jordan: i'll draft the one-pager and send by monday, 2025-01-20. includes co-sell messaging, pricing hooks, and technical bullets.
[05:12] Carlos: and i'll include instructions on registering joint opportunities in the partner portal — we want you to log leads so the commission and co-sell credit flow.
[05:21] Samira: technical question — for medibase they mentioned KMS rotations and audit logs. does redwood integrate with customer KMS?
[05:30] Maya: yes we support major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we can integrate for private deployments. audit logs are available via the console; we'll share sample logs.
[05:40] Priya: sometimes the logs are hard to parse; can you provide a brief doc on what to expect?
[05:45] Maya: yep we'll add a logging map doc.
[05:47] [00:05:48] Liam: for retailworks, we're worried about tail latency on checkout — can you guarantee p99 latency?
[05:57] Maya: guarantees are SLA-backed for dedicated pools; for hosted we publish p95 and latency profiles, and for p99 it depends on burst policies and KV cache warmness. we can work with a dedicated pool or reserve capacity.
[06:12] Jordan: in similar deals we've proposed a hybrid: host initial pilot then move to dedicated for production. that gives them speed to value and a clear path to meet SLAs.
[06:22] Priya: ok that's helpful. for bankcorp we'll ask about data residency — do you have regions in eu/uk?
[06:30] Jordan: yes — eu and uk region support; we'll share an inventory of regions. for private deployments we can be deployed in customer VPCs.
[06:38] Samira: any blocker on demo decks? we have an upcoming sales call with bankcorp on 2025-01-27 — can we get a joint demo with an SE?
[06:47] Jordan: yes, maya can join that call. is 1pm UTC on the 27th ok?
[06:53] Priya: 1pm works. we'll send calendar invite after the call.
[07:00] Carlos: quick note on co-sell attribution — please register the opp in the portal and tag the owner. otherwise it slips through.
[07:08] Priya: will do.
[07:10] [00:07:14] Jordan: moving to risk and blockers — timeline risk is mostly on acme side for getting approvals, and on redwood side for any custom enterprise terms. anything else?
[07:23] Liam: network approvals sometimes add two weeks; i'll flag that. also procurement at bankcorp wants a low liability clause.
[07:31] Jordan: we can work with legal — procurement is always negotiable with commitment. we'll surface a standard liability cap in the SOW.
[07:40] Maya: tech risk — if they want specific quantization/FP16 concerns, we should run a small model compatibility test, but that usually goes smoothly.
[07:51] Samira: do you support model quantization configs?
[07:54] Maya: we support several quantized variants; we'll recommend by workload. we'll include recommendations in the benchmark report.
[08:03] Priya: anything around compliance paperwork — will you give a SOC2 attestation and an incident response contact?
[08:10] Jordan: yes SOC2 + we have incident contacts. i'll share the security package offline.
[08:16] [00:08:18] Carlos: next i'll quickly walk through the partner portal flow — how to log an opp, how to request co-sell support, and where artifacts live. (screen-sharing note: screen noises in transcript may show as garbled)
[08:32] Priya: (overlap) one quick Q — does registering an opp require a deal registration form?
[08:36] Carlos: yes there's a short form in the portal; takes 2-3 minutes. once approved the opp gets a co-sell tag.
[08:43] Priya: perfect.
[08:45] [00:08:48] Jordan: ok to recap — owners: jordan send one-pager + pricing grid (due 2025-01-20); maya run benchmarks (due 2025-01-22); carlos add artifacts to portal and enable pipeline tracking (due 2025-01-18); priya confirm priority accounts (due 2025-01-17).
[09:06] Liam: sounds good. any blockers on the exec intro?
[09:10] Jordan: we need a short mutual intro email and list of execs to include. carlos can help with intros.
[09:19] Samira: i'll ask our sales ops to prepare the account contacts list and share by friday.
[09:25] Priya: one more thing — for the bankcorp security call, can we do a 'mini-A&A' with your security lead? maybe 30 minutes.
[09:33] Jordan: yes we can schedule a 30-minute security deep dive; i'll cc our security lead and propose times next week.
[09:40] [00:09:42] Priya: perfect.
[09:44] Jordan: any final questions?
[09:47] Liam: none from me.
[09:49] Maya: just to confirm benchmarks will include p95/p99, throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
[09:56] Maya: also i'll include a short note on quantization/accuracy tradeoffs.
[09:59] Priya: great.
[10:02] Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.
[10:07] Carlos: thanks everyone.
[10:09] Samira: thanks, bye.

Meeting end.
